title: The checkpoint that resumed from garbage
blurb: Chunks were acknowledged before verification and resumed as weights.
prompt: A training run resumed from a checkpoint whose middle chunk was corrupted, because the draft acknowledged chunks before the store verified checksums and its commit flag trusted a caller-supplied byte count. Review it, fix it, and prove acknowledgments mean durability and commits mean completeness.
aiNote: The draft acknowledges each chunk as soon as it hands it to the store, so corruption is found only in a background pass long after a resume has consumed it, and its commit marker is derived from the caller's declared size rather than the verified chunk set.
testIdea: Corrupt one chunk and assert the upload fails at verification rather than committing; lie about the byte count and assert the commit marker never sets; read the latest checkpoint while an upload is uncommitted and assert it is invisible.
followUps: How would you verify a checkpoint without reading it back fully?
What TTL keeps abandoned uploads from pinning storage forever?
How should a resumed run treat the last verified chunk boundary?
